problem.title: Secret key from every entangled state

question.summary: Many entangled states, including PPT examples, have positive distillable key. No proof covers every entangled state, and no entangled state is known with proved zero distillable key.
question.importance: The answer decides whether entanglement and cryptographic usefulness have the same zero boundary. A zero-key entangled state would separate the two resources.
question.unresolved: Prove that every entangled bipartite state has positive distillable key, or exhibit an entangled state with zero distillable key.

claims.title: Current key-cost theory still treats zero-key entanglement as unresolved
claims.text: The peer-reviewed analysis states its conclusions conditionally on whether entangled states with zero distillable key exist.

claims.title: Some PPT bound-entangled states contain secret key
claims.text: Horodecki and collaborators construct bound-entangled states with positive distillable key, a major positive subclass that does not settle the universal quantifier.
